role_inventory.role: Private Packed trait and fixed-width type-specific codec
role_inventory.trace: Packed names the actual common operation: a value of statically declared word width can append its u32 words and rebuild Self from exactly that many words. Sized supports return Self. This is a coherent local wire-format helper, not an additional application position/triangle/binding authority. Shared implementation can encode records of different meaning without collapsing their semantic owners. No extra quantity/index enum or public encoding framework justified.

The Vec2 and Vec3 numerical records use f32::to_bits/from_bits; topology triangle triples retain u32 integers directly. Both float3 and triangle3 occupy3words but use different T and corresponding pack/unpack paths. The generic typed field supplies interpretation; record bytes are not self-describing and width alone does not identify semantic role. Existing named SettledDrape fields retain positions, UV and faces separately, so same representation does not authorize merging them or adding duplicate position/triangle owners at the wire adapter.

SurfaceBinding implements Packed WORDS6: triangle ordinal,2barycentric floats and3local-frame-offset floats in fixed sequence. It names unlike roles before serialization and reconstructs that same record after decoding. Private named semantic record owns this distinction; homogeneous u32 word buffer is only native representation. This differs from typed float/triangle arrays even though all emit u32 words.

role_inventory.role: Encoded record words, bytes and base64 text
role_inventory.trace: serialize<T> allocates a word vector using values.len*WORDS, appends each T record, converts every word explicitly to little-endian bytes and feeds actual byte payload to STANDARD.encode, then Serializer.serialize_str. Words, byte buffer and text have distinct wire responsibilities; no application String is retained across semantic processing here. Serde field adapter is the exact external text boundary. Endianness and one-string shape are intentional native schema, not arbitrary text constants needing an application enum.

role_inventory.role: Decode-to-arity admission versus semantic value admission
role_inventory.trace: deserialize asks D for String, STANDARD.decode returns bytes/errors mapped to D::Error::custom, record width is WORDS*size_of u32, and non-integral record byte count is rejected. Then four-byte chunks decode with from_le_bytes, and chunks_exact(WORDS) feeds T::unpack. For actual reached widths2/3/6 this ensures every indexed unpack receives its fixed arity. It does not guarantee finite floats, triangle bounds, paired vector cardinality or topology association: SettledDrape.validate explicitly owns those selected semantic checks after capture/when invoked. Do not move those unrelated application checks into the generic codec or claim deriving Deserialize calls them automatically.

role_inventory.role: Scalar word count versus byte stride and record population
role_inventory.trace: WORDS counts native u32 units per record, record is bytes per record, values.len is record population and bytes.len is encoded buffer length. Their numerical relation is explicit at adapter; they are not interchangeable physical units or a reason to create new public counter wrappers. All reached implementations have positive fixed width. No blanket guarantee for future zero/inconsistent WORDS implementation, capacity arithmetic overflow, resource limits or arbitrary huge inputs.

role_inventory.role: Empty serialized collection versus valid saved garment
role_inventory.trace: Empty byte array is an integral number of positive-width records and decodes to empty Vec. That is a valid generic codec result; saved garment owner separately requires nonempty bindings/faces and matching positions/UV. Imposing nonempty in this common adapter would conflate shape decoding with unrelated field/content policy. No unsupported generic bounds invented.

role_inventory.role: Native codec error versus application status
role_inventory.trace: Base64 or shape errors become generic D::Error, with diagnostic byte/record count text. This is native decoding failure evidence; it does not introduce a closed gameplay status vocabulary or another saved-drape state. Standard codec acceptance details are not asserted from an uninspected external implementation.
